items.item_text: cover letter
references
The ideal candidate should hold a California pharmacist license, have clinical training, and possess at least five years of experience in a school of pharmacy.
The candidate must possess a doctorate (PharmD and/or PhD), training in pharmacy or a related field, and experience in curricular and programmatic administration within pharmacy education.
and the capacity to advance and support the School’s educational, service, research, and clinical missions.

Coordinates shared faculty responsibilities, including academic personnel reviews, teaching assignments, workload. In conjunction with the Assistant Dean of Experiential Education, coordinates the site placement of clinical faculty.
Leads the recruitment, retention, supervision, and evaluation of PharmD program faculty, including conducting regular performance reviews and providing constructive feedback.
Develops and oversees the faculty mentoring and professional development programs, fostering a collegial culture of excellence.
Coordinates peer-evaluation of teaching and student evaluation of faculty.
Oversees the faculty advising program for students, including advisor assignments and support.
Oversees faculty service, including committee membership, leadership appointments, and the assignment of faculty advisors to student clubs and organizations.
Supports and participates in accreditation activities, as required, in collaboration with the other Associate and Assistant Deans and the Dean of the School.

Collaborates with the other Associate and Assistant Deans and the Dean of the School to ensure the quality of curricular offerings, promote student success, and foster a culture of assessment and innovation.
Partners with the Assistant Dean of Assessment and Pharmacy Education on matters related to student progression.
Supports the School’s PharmD admissions activities, such as recruitment events and candidate interviews.
Provides collaborative leadership in fostering a collegial environment.

In partnership with the Dean, Assistant Dean of Assessment and Pharmacy Education, and the Assistant Dean of Experiential Education, ensures that syllabi syllabi for didactic and experiential courses are developed and maintained.
Maintains and strengthens partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to expand practice and research opportunities and to secure external funding.
Teaches and provides service as appropriate to the faculty appointment and areas of expertise.
Conducts scholarship that advances the theory and practice of pharmacy, pharmacy education, and faculty and personnel development.
Performs other duties as assigned by the Dean.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to effectively communicate, both verbally and in writing, and to respond promptly to inquiries and emerging issues.
Excellent time management skills and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to work as a member of a team of highly motivated and experienced individuals.
Honesty, integrity, and commitment to maintaining high professional standards.
Ability to handle multiple priorities while reliably following through and delivering work on time.
Proven ability to build consensus and hold faculty accountable, including delivering candid feedback on performance and navigating difficult conversations with tact and professionalism.
Innovative, entrepreneurial, and a strategic thinker.
